name: Beaujolais

rules.yield_base: 68 hl/ha for white, 60 for rosé and red

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
A wine made within weeks of harvest and released at 12:01 am on the third Thursday of November.
The middle tier, from 38 villages in the north of the region, with the crus, such as Fleurie, above it.
keyfacts: There are three tiers: Beaujolais, Beaujolais-Villages from the northern half of the area, and Cru Beaujolais with ten crus.

notes: Most Beaujolais reds are light in color, fruity and floral, and made to drink young. Villages and cru wines are deeper and more structured, and can keep for several years.
Beaujolais Nouveau is released on the third Thursday of November. It is fresh and fruity, and meant to drink within a few months.
Producers usually use a semi-carbonic style of fermentation to keep the fruit.

blurb.text: A French appellation between Mâcon and Lyon, best known for light-bodied red wine from Gamay, a thin-skinned, low-tannin grape. White, made only from Chardonnay, is about 4 percent of production. Crus within it include Morgon, Fleurie, Moulin-à-Vent and Brouilly.
